html:
1Ways to manage Azure

All of these tools send the same requests to Azure Resource Manager, so you can use whichever fits the job.

Tool Style Best for
Azure portal Web graphical interface Learning, exploring, one-off tasks, dashboards
Azure Cloud Shell Browser-based command line (Bash or PowerShell) Quick commands from any device, no install
Azure CLI Cross-platform command-line tool (az) Scripts and automation, many platforms
Azure PowerShell PowerShell cmdlets (Az module) Automation for people who use PowerShell
ARM templates / Bicep Declarative files (infrastructure as code) Repeatable, consistent deployments
REST APIs and SDKs Beyond the study guide Code Custom applications

2The Azure portal

The Azure portal is a web-based graphical console for building, managing and monitoring Azure resources.

  • Works in a browser, no installation, usually with point-and-click steps.
  • Offers customizable dashboards, search and a view of all resources.
  • Great for learning and occasional tasks; not ideal for repeating the same work many times (manual steps are slow and can differ each time).

3Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell

Azure Cloud Shell Azure CLI Azure PowerShell
What Browser-based shell hosted by Azure Cross-platform command-line tool Module of cmdlets for PowerShell
Install? No (opens from the portal) Yes (Windows, macOS, Linux) Yes (Windows, macOS, Linux)
Language Bash or PowerShell Commands start with az Cmdlets named like Get-AzVM
Typical use Run quick commands anywhere Scripts and automation Scripts and automation
  • Cloud Shell comes with Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell already installed and is authenticated with your account. It keeps files in an Azure Files share (a storage account is used for persistence).
  • CLI and PowerShell can do the same tasks; the choice is about preference, not capability.
  • Both support scripts, so they make work repeatable and automatable.
Exam tip

. No installation, in the browser → Cloud Shell. az commands → Azure CLI. Get-Az... cmdlets → Azure PowerShell. Graphical → portal.

4Azure Arc

Azure Arc extends Azure management and services to resources outside Azure: on-premises, in other clouds and at the edge.

With Arc you can:

  • Project servers, Kubernetes clusters and databases into Azure as Arc-enabled resources.
  • Apply Azure Policy, tags, RBAC, monitoring and Defender for Cloud to them like Azure resources.
  • Run some Azure services (such as Azure data services) anywhere.
Exam tip

. "Manage on-premises or other-cloud servers from Azure with a single control plane" → Azure Arc. It supports hybrid and multicloud management.

5Infrastructure as code (IaC)

Infrastructure as code means defining your infrastructure in files and deploying it by running them, instead of clicking in a portal.

Benefit Meaning
Consistency The same file gives the same result every time
Repeatability Create test, staging and production the same way
Speed and automation Deploy a whole environment in minutes
Version control Store the files in source control, review and roll back
Documentation The file itself describes the environment

Two styles: declarative (you describe the end state: "I want these resources", and the platform works out how) and imperative (you list the steps). ARM templates and Bicep are declarative; scripts with CLI or PowerShell are usually imperative.

6Azure Resource Manager and ARM templates

Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is the deployment and management service for Azure. Every request from the portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs or templates goes through ARM, which authenticates, authorizes and then performs the action.

ARM lets you:

  • Manage resources as a group (resource groups) and apply access control, tags, locks and policy.
  • Deploy many resources together in the right order with dependencies.
  • Get a consistent experience across all tools.

ARM templates are JSON files that declare the resources to deploy.

Feature Meaning
Declarative Describe what you want, not the steps
Idempotent Deploying the same template again gives the same result, with no duplicates
Repeatable and reusable Use parameters to change names, sizes or regions
Orchestration ARM deploys resources in parallel or in order based on dependencies
Modular Split big deployments into linked or nested templates

Bicep is a simpler language that compiles to ARM templates. Beyond the study guide

Exam tip

. "Deploy the same environment repeatedly and consistently" → ARM template (IaC). "Every request goes through one management layer" → ARM. JSON + declarative + idempotent → ARM template.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors needs to deploy identical test and production environments again and again with no manual differences. What should it use?

  • AThe Azure portal with the same clicks each time
  • BAzure Advisor recommendations
  • CA resource lock on both environments
  • DARM templates (infrastructure as code)
Show the answer

Answer: D. Templates are declarative, repeatable and consistent.

S2An administrator wants to run Azure commands from a browser on any computer without installing software. What fits?

  • AAzure Cloud Shell
  • BAzure CLI installed locally
  • CAzure PowerShell installed locally
  • DAzure Arc
Show the answer

Answer: A. Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell with CLI and PowerShell ready.

S3A company wants to manage its on-premises Windows and Linux servers with Azure Policy and Defender for Cloud. Which service enables this?

  • AVNet peering
  • BAzure Arc
  • CAzure Data Box
  • DAzure DNS
Show the answer

Answer: B. Azure Arc projects non-Azure resources into Azure so Azure management tools apply.

S4Which service receives every management request, whether it comes from the portal, CLI or a template?

  • AAzure Resource Manager
  • BAzure Monitor
  • CAzure Policy
  • DAzure DNS
Show the answer

Answer: A. ARM is the single management layer for Azure resources.

S5Which statement about ARM templates is true?

  • AThey are imperative scripts that list every step to run in sequence
  • BThey are declarative JSON files and can be deployed repeatedly with the same result
  • CThey can only be used in the portal, never from the command line
  • DThey replace resource groups and subscriptions
Show the answer

Answer: B. ARM templates declare the desired state and are idempotent.

S6Which commands belong to Azure CLI?

  • ACommands such as Get-AzVM
  • BOnly graphical clicks
  • COnly JSON files
  • DCommands starting with az
Show the answer

Answer: D. Azure CLI commands start with az. Get-AzVM is an Azure PowerShell cmdlet.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Which tool is a web graphical interface?

Show the answer

The Azure portal.

R2Which two shells are available in Cloud Shell?

Show the answer

Bash and PowerShell.

R3What does Azure Arc do?

Show the answer

Extends Azure management to on-premises, other clouds and the edge.

R4What is infrastructure as code?

Show the answer

Defining infrastructure in files that are deployed automatically, for consistent and repeatable results.

R5What does idempotent mean for a template?

Show the answer

Deploying it again gives the same result with no duplicates.

R6What is Bicep?

Show the answer

A simpler language that compiles to ARM templates.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Portal web GUI; learn and one-off tasks
Cloud Shell browser shell, Bash or PowerShell, no install, CLI and PowerShell included
CLI vs PowerShell az commands vs Get-Az... cmdlets; both cross-platform and scriptable
Azure Arc manage on-premises, multicloud and edge resources from Azure
IaC infrastructure in files: consistent, repeatable, fast, versioned; declarative vs imperative
ARM the management layer all tools use; groups, access control, locks, policy
ARM templates declarative JSON, idempotent, parameters, dependencies; Bicep compiles to them
